counterfactual_missing_items: No significant family history of neuromuscular disorders
decisive_items: Delayed motor development in early childhood
progressive muscle weakness starting in lower limbs then upper limbs
response.rationale: R2 is the champion because it has the most comprehensive support from the patient's history, including very low birth weight, delayed motor development, and progressive muscle weakness, which are all consistent with Congenital Muscular Dystrophy. R1 is the runner-up, but it is less likely due to the normal sensory and cerebellar examinations, which contradict the typical presentation of Spinal Muscular Atrophy.

rejected.why: Normal EMG at rest with no electrical myotonia contradicts the typical presentation of Myotonic Dystrophy.
